documents.t: Step 1: In the portal’s menu tab, go to Admin Center. Step 2: Under Admin Center select Advanced Migration. You will be taken to the installation screen. A preview of the Installation Screen is given below:
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Installation Guide/Advanced Migration - Installation Screen/About Advanced Migration- Installation Screen

documents.t: The installation screen is used to install or update external apps. This includes the app’s folder that will be saved in the closedmodules folder and its zip will be extracted in cdn_app. Apart from this, the installation screen does the following tasks in the background: Update madm_app table. Update the Flavor folder in the closedmodules folder. Update the Flavor zip in the cdn_app folder. Create/Update Tables for that App and its dependent app. Install Config for that App. The screen will have a table which contains all information relevant to the app. Following is a list of columns in the app installation screen like the App name. Components Description App Name of the app. BOL Version BOL version used by the app. Version A version of the app. Is External It is a component of the app. If is_external is marked as false then the app is in closedmodules, if marked as true then the app is in cdn_app. Dependant App Shows the dependent app information of a particular app with the dependent app name and version. Created On Shows the date app was created. Landscape The landscape where the apps are present.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Installation Guide/Advanced Migration - Installation Screen/About Advanced Migration- Installation Screen

documents.t: To install an app follow the following steps: Click the Upload App button on the top left of the screen to select the zip file and press OK. Note: zip name should be proper for eg:- app_version.zip. Then a popup screen will appear that will give relevant details related to the app, if the app is already there in the madm_app table then it will ask for an install. If it's not there then it will ask for an update. On click of install or update, madm_app will be updated, tables for that app will be generated and the app zip will be placed inside closed modules with extracted files.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/Installation Guide/Advanced Migration - Installation Screen/About Advanced Migration- Installation Screen

documents.t: There is one download button that lets you download any app‘s zip from the current server (cdn_app) where the application is running. Note:- If the app is internal (i.e. r_is_external = 0), it will be downloaded from the cdn_app/release_build folder (i.e. prodBuild zip). If the app is external (i.e. r_is_external = 1), it will be downloaded from the cdn_app folder (i.e. devBuild zip). Whenever you make any changes in an existing app that has already been moved using the Advanced app mover; You need to change the app version make the changes in the app and then move the app. This will help in triggering the Update Schema through the URL. (For more information related to update schema and fixed schema through URL, read this article.

documents.t: A plugin is an add-on code which provides functionality to cordova app or more precisely cordova web view to communicate with native components or in easy words it is used to provide additional features to cordova app. There are various plugins , few example below Phonegap-plugin-barcodescanner - to scan barcode Cordova-plugin-file-transfer - to upload and download files For adding plugin run command cordova plugin add <plugin-name> For removing plugin run command cordova plugin rm <plugin-name> Example - Cordova plugin add Phonegap-plugin-barcodescanner Note : Sometimes plugins are not compatible with dependent plugins . Then we have to use - - force at the end of command to add plugins forcefully. Example: Cordova plugin add Phonegap-plugin-barcodescanner - -force

documents.t: When a new Klobase version is detected, the Klobase Update Required tab opens in VS Code. It shows the Current Workspace, the Previous Klobase Version and the New Klobase Version. documents.t: A .certSigningRequest file is a critical part of the certificate generation process in iOS development. It is used to create a code-signing certificate, which is necessary for signing your iOS apps for distribution via In-House or Ad Hoc methods. The CSR file contains information about the developer or the organization, including the public key, which is used by Apple to generate the appropriate signing certificate.If you want to create a new Certificate, then follow the steps below. Open the keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Request a Certificate From a Certificate Authority as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Fill the below details as shown in the below screenshot. The user's email address plays an indirect role in the code-signing process since it is linked to your Apple Developer account and included in the signing certificate's metadata. While the Keychain holds the signing certificate and private key, it does not store the email address in plain text. Instead, the email is embedded within the certificate's metadata, which identifies the developer or organization. In short: Email is used to identify the developer in the signing certificate. Keychain stores the certificate and private key needed for signing the app, enabling secure app distribution and code signing. The CA Email Address is a part of the Issuer information within a certificate and provides a way to contact the Certificate Authority that issued the certificate. It serves as a point of contact for issues related to the certificate, such as validation, renewal, or revocation. You can find the CA's email address in the certificate metadata, which can be inspected in various tools like Keychain Access on macOS or by viewing the certificate details in a web browser. Ad Hoc: Choose Ad Hoc distribution if you have a small group of testers or specific clients who need to test or review your app before release. documents.t: Provisioning profiles are essential for code signing, testing, and distributing iOS apps. They serve as the bridge between certificates, devices, and apps, enabling you to securely install and run apps on real devices and distribute them via different channels, such as internal enterprise apps, Ad Hoc distribution, and the App Store. Proper management of Provisioning Profiles ensures smooth app development, testing, and deployment processes.If you want to create a new profile then follow the steps below. Select in house and click on continue. Provide the Identifier id which you created in the previous step and click on continue. Select the certificate you created and click on continue. Give your profile name and click on generate.
